data.body:
The first Dr. Lurié Skincare shelf is deliberately small: one daytime barrier serum, one night cream, and a few practical supports around them.

This is a mock storefront for pre-launch testing. The promise is not miracle language. It is fewer decisions, clearer labels, and a plain path for people who came to skin care late and do not want to be manipulated.
data.heading: Premium skin care for late starters who are tired of being sold confusion.

data.heading: How this shelf earns trust before it asks for money
items: A two-product core shelf first, not a maze of bundles.
Large, readable packaging and plain product names.
No miracle claims, fear copy, or invented urgency.
Paid PDFs stay separate from product sales so education can challenge the offer.
Mock pricing is visible early, because mistrust grows in the dark.

data.heading: Questions a skeptical buyer should ask

items.a: Because the late starter does not need a wall of choices. The first offer should prove the discipline of the brand before the brand earns permission to expand.
No. This is pre-launch mock stock for testing the site, offer shape, and audience fit before go-live.
The audience mistrusts the industry. A strong education layer lets Dr. Lurié Skincare sell with receipts, not pressure.

data.body: Short updates on the two-SKU launch, ingredient reasoning, testing notes, and the PDFs that explain when not to buy.
